draft.title: The siege of Tobruk
card: Tobruk was a port in Libya, in North Africa. In 1941 it was held by Allied troops, and German and Italian forces surrounded it.
A siege is when an enemy surrounds a place and tries to force its defenders to give up. Supplies had to come in by sea.
Australian troops made up most of the defenders. They held out for around eight months, from April to December 1941.
The defenders were nicknamed the Rats of Tobruk. They lived in dugouts and caves. The name was meant as an insult by German radio, but they took it as a badge of pride.
draft.remember: Surrounded and short of supplies, the Australians held Tobruk for months and turned an insult into a proud name.

opts: An enemy surrounds a place to force its defenders to give up
A fast attack by aircraft on a port or city
A retreat by an army from a place it cannot hold
A battle fought along a narrow track through jungle
a.why: In a siege the attackers surround a place and try to wear the defenders down. A fast air raid is a different kind of attack, and it does not involve surrounding a place and holding it over months.
a.clue: Think about what it means for a place to be surrounded.

b.q: Why were the Australian defenders at Tobruk called the Rats of Tobruk?
opts: German radio used it as an insult and they took it as pride
They were named after the rats found in Libyan ports
The Australian government gave them the name as an award
They hid from the enemy by living in ships in the harbour
b.why: The name began as an insult from German radio. The defenders lived in dugouts and caves, and they adopted the name proudly. It was not an official award from the government.
b.clue: Who first used the name, and what did the defenders do with it?

a.best: An enemy surrounds a place to force its defenders to give up

b.best: German radio used it as an insult and they took it as pride

problems.detail: 'They held out for around eight months, from April to December 1941' implies the Australians defended Tobruk for the whole siege. Most of the Australian 9th Division was withdrawn by sea between August and October 1941 and replaced by British, Polish and Czechoslovak troops. Only one Australian battalion (2/13th) stayed until the siege was lifted in late November or December. It should say the siege lasted about eight months and Australians held it for most of that time.
